lectures.title: How can Achilles ever catch the tortoise? Zeno's paradox
Can a full hotel take one more guest? Hilbert's Hotel and Cantor's diagonal
Can one ball become two? The Banach–Tarski paradox
Does the set of all sets that don't contain themselves contain itself? Russell's paradox
What is the smallest number you can't describe in a few words? Berry's paradox
Can maths prove everything? Gödel's incompleteness theorems
Can a program tell whether any program will finish? Turing's halting problem
Can a surprise be announced? The surprise exam paradox
When does sand become a heap? The sorites paradox
Would you pay a fortune for an infinitely valuable game? The St Petersburg paradox
One box or two? Newcomb's problem
Can any voting rule be fair? Arrow's impossibility theorem

quiz.question: Which of these sums has a finite total?
Guests arrive, each holding an endless list of coin tosses: heads, tails, tails, heads… Can the full hotel give every one a room?
A friend splits the surface of a sphere into a few pieces and, only by turning them, builds two spheres the same size. What must be true of the pieces?
A library makes a catalogue of every catalogue that doesn't list itself. Should that catalogue list itself?
choices: Yes, but only in a footnote
No, it must leave itself out

quiz.question: A rulebook one megabyte long proves that a certain string needs a program over a gigabyte. What follows?
A friend builds a new, consistent rulebook for arithmetic with a million axioms, all listed. What can you say?
A company says its new tool can check any program, on any input, however long it runs, and always tell correctly whether it will ever stop. What should you think?
A manager announces a surprise fire drill on one of the next three days. Two days pass with no drill. What can staff honestly say that evening?
choices: Tomorrow, or the manager was wrong

quiz.question: Pluck one hair from a full head: still not bald. Do it 100,000 times: still not bald? Most logicians blame which step?
A $10 ticket wins $1 million with a chance of 1 in 50,000, otherwise nothing. Its average payout is $20. Why might a sensible person with $1,000 refuse?
Flossers live longer, so tonight you floss, though you know flossing does nothing for your health. Which box-taker reasons like you?
A five-member board picks one of four sites by votes in pairs, and the chair sets the order. What should worry you most?
choices: Nothing: each vote is a fair majority
The order may decide the winner
Arrow says it can't decide at all
